quote: The following results discuss the variability ordering of lifetimes of parallel systems with independent heterogeneous GMW components in terms of the reversed hazard rate order. Theorem 1. Let X_1, ..., X_n be a set of independent random variables with X_i ∼ GMW(α_i, γ, λ, β)، i = 1, ..., n. Further، let X*_1, ..., X*_n be another set of independent random variables with X*_i ∼ GMW(α*_i, γ, λ, β)، i = 1, ..., n. If (α_1, ..., α_n) ⪯^w (α*_1, ..., α*_n)، then X_{n:n} ≤_rh X*_{n:n}.

quote: The following result considers the comparison of the lifetimes of two series systems in terms of the usual stochastic order when the shape parameters (α) of the distribution of component lifetimes of a system is weakly majorized by the shape parameters (α*) of the other system. Theorem 7. Let X_1, ..., X_n be a set of independent random variables with X_i ∼ GMW(α_i, γ, λ, β), i = 1, ..., n. Further, let X*_1, ..., X*_n be another set of independent random variables with X*_i ∼ GMW(α*_i, γ, λ, β), i = 1, ..., n. Then, (i) for (α_1, ..., α_n) ⪯_w (α*_1, ..., α*_n), we have X_{1:n} ≥_st X*_{1:n} if β ≥ 1; (ii) (α_1, ..., α_n) ⪯^w (α*_1, ..., α*_n), we have X_{1:n} ≤_st X*_{1:n} if 0 < β ≤ 1.

quote: Naturally, one may wonder whether the following statement is actually also true: For 0 < β ≤ 1, (α_1, ..., α_n) ⪯^p (α*_1, ..., α*_n) gives rise to the usual stochastic order between X_{1:n} and X*_{1:n}. The following example gives negative answer to these two conjecture. Example 3. Let (X_1, X_2) ((X*_1, X*_2)) be a vector of independent heterogeneous GMW random variables. Set β = 0.5, γ = 2 and λ = 3. For (α_1, α_2) = (2, 3) ⪯^p (1, 5.5) = (α*_1, α*_2), X_{1:2} ≥_st X*_{1:2}, as can be seen in Fig. 3 (A); however, for (α_1, α_2) = (1.1, 6) ⪯^p (1, 2.25) = (α*_1, α*_2), X_{1:2} ≤_st X*_{1:2}, as can be seen in Fig. 3 (B) So, (α_1, α_2) ⪯^p (α*_1, α*_2) implies neither X_{1:2} ≤_st X*_{1:2} nor X_{1:2} ≥_st X*_{1:2} for 0 < β ≤ 1. quote: Before going into the details, let us recall one important general family of distributions. We say that random variable X belongs to the Exponentiated Scale (ES) family of distributions if X ∼ H(x) = [G(λx)]^α, where α, λ > 0 and G is called the baseline distribution function which we assume that is absolutely continuous. In the sequel, we denote this family by ES(α, λ). Bashkar et al. (2017) proved the following general result. Theorem 11. Suppose for i = 1, ..., n, X_i ∼ ES(α_i, λ) and X*_i ∼ ES(α*_i, λ) share a common Archimedean survival copula with generator ϕ. Then, X_{1:n} ≤_st X*_{1:n} if (α_1, ..., α_n) ⪰^w (α*_1, ..., α*_n).
